readme:
# JSNode package services

`@red-cup-engineering/jsnode-package-services-section` 0.1.0 admits,
projects, and creates JSNode operation packages from a closed specification.
Its package CLI is `jsnode-package admit`, `jsnode-package project`, and
`jsnode-package create`. The public atomic subpaths are the corresponding
operations, `./translate-markdown-jsnode-operation-package-specification`, and
`./jsnode-package-dialect`.

## Package shape

Version 2 models a topic package, whose name is independent of an individual
operation or title. A package may contain multiple operations described as
`JsnodeOperationArguments`, common modules in `src/`, one script per operation
in `scripts/`, and one topic CLI at `apps/<topic>-cli.mjs`. Each script exports
one operation and has an NDJSON command guard generated from that operation.
The package also exposes each atomic operation through an explicit import
subpath.

The package creator admits only generated artifacts in `src/`, `scripts/`,
`apps/`, `data/records/`, and `schema/`; runtime data is excluded. It preserves
the work order's source digest and spans, with traceability from requirements
and prohibitions to their projections and acceptance obligations.

Creation assays syntax and authored tests, then every operation's direct
NDJSON, import, and application faces from a tarball installed in a clean
directory. Ordinary tests do not publish to a registry. Version 1 work orders
remain accepted.

## Markdown work-order dialect

The v2 dialect is defined by `src/jsnode-package.mjs` and its translator. Its
`Package` JSON has `version: 2`, `topic`, package identity and version,
license, dependencies, and development dependencies. `Sources` contains mjs
fences with `path=src/<name>.mjs`; `Operations` contains JSON
`JsnodeOperationArguments` fences; and each `Examples` JSON fence has a
`name` and an `operation=scripts/<command>.mjs` attribute. The closed work
order also carries requirements, prohibitions, laws, standards, questions,
tests, and traceability.

## Destination behavior

Creation requires an absent destination. An existing destination is refused
with `DESTINATION_EXISTS`; in-place revision is not supported.
